newsitem.title: UK: Coffee-Demand turns brisk as buyers pay up.
newsitem.headline: Coffee-Demand turns brisk as buyers pay up.

text.p: Physical coffee markets saw brisk demand for nearby and new crops as buyers reluctantly matched higher offer prices with producers firmly in the driver's seat.
"It's a seller's market," said one. "Roasters are buying against May still."
Producers have been pushing to sell coffee priced against New York's May contract which commands a hefty premium over second-position July. But roasters favour the latter.
On Tuesday, the May premium stood at 18 cents a lb.
Concerns of a squeeze on the May contract, which enters the first notice day on April 22, sent the prices to over $2.00 mark in early Tuesday business.
The latest rally was also fuelled by news Colombia had closed registrations for May-June shipments and a fresh port strike in Brazil.
A possible new Colombian truck drivers strike due within a week also threatened to disrupt supplies and buoy prices further.
Colombia has said its 1996/97 (April/May) crop has fallen to 10 million 60-kg bags from about 14 million a year earlier.
In Europe, traders noted good demand for nearby coffee for shipment in May, June and July but availabilities from Central America were basically non-existent.
"We have also been able to move fair quantities of new arabica crop for October-December shipments," said one Swiss trader. "There's also been growing demand for robustas."
Brazil prices have varied widely with those holding stocks calling the shots.
"It's not a clear market for Brazil now," said one.
Others said differentials for robustas however were weakening on the advent of the main Indonesian harvest.
Ugandan robusta sales have dried up as the crop was nearing its end and also due to the fact that the internal prices were higher than the international prices.
African arabicas especially the high quality Zaire and Rwanda origins were still enjoying good demand.
Following differentials for some origins:
Brazil 3/4 medium good beans 3 cents/lb under NY's July
Costa Rica hard bean (June) 15 cents over NY July
Kenya AB FAQ main crop 110-115 cents over NY July
Kenya AA FAQ 115-120 cents over NY July
Ivory Coast Grade 2 (Apr/May) $40 under London CIF
Uganda Screen 15 $15 under London CIF Europe
Indonesian EK1 (April/May) $220 under London FOB
-- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
